result.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
result.summary: Scaling embedding capacity alongside Transformer computation is an emerging trend in language models. This trend makes high compression rates increasingly useful. Hence, we study extreme compression of Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE), which follow this trend and account for 35.2% of the parameters of Gemma 4 E4B. At such rates, conventional quantizers give each token-layer vector its own code of only a few bytes. We instead develop OPTIC (Output-Path-fitted, Token-shared Indexed Codes), which stores one quantized code tuple per token and decodes it at every layer with a layer-specific affine decoder. Codes and decoders are fitted to the PLE output path rather than to the stored vectors. At about $100\times$ PLE compression of bfloat16 (BF16) E4B, OPTIC retains an aggregate 97.8% of the uncompressed model's performance across seven benchmarks, whereas product quantization, the strongest of six conventional baselines, retains 66.3%. At $594\times$ and $1,002\times$ PLE compression of BF16 E4B, OPTIC retains 90.5% and 84.1%. On the official E4B release with 4-bit linear weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16), OPTIC retains 96.9% at about $100\times$ PLE compression. During inference at about $100\times$ PLE compression, BF16 E4B uses 29.7% less GPU memory than with uncompressed PLE at the same key-value cache size, while running at most 0.40% slower.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 OPTIC，把 Per-Layer Embeddings 极致压缩为每 token 一组共享量化码，再用逐层专用的仿射解码器还原；在约 100 倍压缩下保留 Gemma 4 E4B 约 97.8% 的聚合性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 「token 级共享码 + 逐层专用解码器、且拟合到输出路径」可供核查跨层 latent 信息的共享与深度相关读出方式，以及按输出贡献安排监督的做法；但它针对静态嵌入压缩而非推理期状态，仅为方法线索。
